scenario: A scholarly-analytics brief features only journals that remain indexed and show citation growth above 30%. Publishers use the brief's average to estimate typical citation growth across all journals.

data.description: Only surviving journals with growth above 30 percentage points are included. Growth is Normal with sigma 12 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean citation-growth mu across all journals and (b) the fraction of journals featured.
naive_answer: Typical citation growth is about 35.6 points because that is the brief average.
naive_trap: The brief includes only upper-tail surviving journals.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.3.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(30-mu)/12; return mu+12*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-35.64
mu=brentq(eq,-100,29.99)
frac=norm.sf((30-mu)/12)
assert abs(mu-14.4)<0.8 and abs(frac-0.0968)<0.005
